text:
olivia: Brain dump: for airgapped model bundles I'm leaning toward an index-first delivery + a tiny proof-stream endpoint so the node can verify/apply as bytes arrive. Pros: faster warmup, selective shard fetch. Cons: verifier complexity, signer/epoch edgecases. Anyone experimented with this pattern?

deepak: We've prototyped something similar for huge weights. Key constraints:
- index must be cryptographically bound to the payload (signed, include epoch)
- proofs need to be incremental (so verifier doesn't require whole file)
- resume must be idempotent on powercuts

deepak: Rough index example (compact):
```json
{
  "bundle": "redwood-bundle-2026-11",
  "version": "index-v1",
  "epoch": "2026-11-12T22:00:00Z",
  "signer": "onprem-signer-rot1",
  "parts": [
    {"name": "weights/shard-0", "len": 2147483648, "merkle_root": "f1e2..."},
    {"name": "weights/shard-1", "len": 2147483648, "merkle_root": "a4b3..."}
  ],
  "signature": "BASE64SIG"
}
```

jane: From operator side we need explicit persisted state: apply_cursor (byte offset), verified_root (per-part), last_epoch_seen, activation_state (pending|active|failed). Without that you can't safely resume or garbage collect partials. Also need a tombstone marker for aborted activations to avoid half-applied cruft.

samir: UX note: allow two activation strategies: "stream-apply" (progressive) and "atomic-swap" (download full image and swap). Default should be stream-apply for capacity-limited nodes, but operator should be able to fallback.

olivia: Good. How do we handle a mid-apply index rotation (new bundle published with same name)? We should probably bind verifier to the index epoch on first fetch. If epoch changes mid-apply, either continue with bound epoch or abort; automatic switch is risky.

rafael: Security: require signer_id + epoch in index. For customers with KMS/HSM, support verifying against a customer public keyset. Also add short-lived activation_token signed by local HSM to tie activation to node_id+bundle_id (prevent replay on different nodes).

deepak: Proof streaming API idea: /bundles/<id>/parts/<part>/proofs?range=0-1048575 that returns newline-delimited records: base64(payload_chunk)+\t+base64(leaf_proof). Support HTTP range header too so curl works:
```
curl -H "Range: bytes=0-1048575" https://registry.local/bundles/redwood-bundle-2026-11/parts/weights/shard-0/proofs
```
Verifier flow (pseudo):
1) fetch and verify index.json signature, record epoch
2) choose parts, open proof stream(s)
3) for each record: verify leaf proof -> write chunk to staging -> update apply_cursor
4) when part complete: verify merkle root -> set part verified
5) after all parts verified: flip activation_state to active and run post-activate hook

jane: Add apply_window (default 30m) with exponential retry. If window expires operator marks activation failed and either revert to previous active image or require manual recover. Document powercut scenarios heavily.

rafael: Also: signer rotation model. Index should include signer_chain_id or key_version so operator can reject older signatures. Provide a GRACE_PERIOD policy for very short key transitions but default to strict reject.

samir: We should version index schema (index-v1, index-v2) so older operators can at least detect incompatibility and fall back to full-image download.

ci-bot: build-bot: note: artifact-generator now emits compact indices + per-part merkle roots. example build: https://ci.redwood.example/builds/5039 :rocket:

olivia: Next actions I propose:
- RFC for index-v1 + streaming API (include HTTP range and record framing)
- PoC verifier lib (go) demonstrating resume and activation_token flow
- operator CRD additions: apply_cursor, part_verified[], activation_state, apply_window, bound_epoch
- security doc for signer rotation and activation_token design
I'll draft RFC and tag @deepak for PoC, @jane for CRD fields, @rafael for security review. Thanks! :thumbsup:
